result.scientific_strategy:
## abd93958-a0b2-4d26-b212-96ebeb401d22 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the unchanged official two-joint-arm task. The fresh PPO baseline in experiment 1 reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.0% on the protected task-reference panel at checkpoint-100352, while its endpoint regressed on both panels. Experiment 2 transferred that checkpoint and expanded training coverage to the official 6–20 cm radius range; its selected checkpoint reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.5% on the task-reference panel. Experiment 3 transferred the same lineage and added joint-configuration progress shaping, but its measured mid-run checkpoints matched experiment 2 and retained the same task-reference failures, while its endpoint regressed to 96.5%/97.0%. The campaign therefore has a near-objective policy with a fixed-panel gain but no robust cross-panel attainment; experiment 2 checkpoint-100352 remains the strongest measured development policy. This synthesis is provisional memory for reassessment, not a prescribed next action.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, rather than logged reward or training success, is the policy-progress signal. All three experiments identify checkpoint selection as important: later training reduced logged dynamics and did not improve measured success. Experiment 2 reduced the task-reference failures from four to three, recovering two short-radius negative-angle cases, but left failures at 9.4–9.9 cm and about -123 to -128 degrees plus one 18.2 cm case at -154.8 degrees. Experiment 3's 80,896- and 100,352-step candidates preserved exactly those three task-reference failures and the same six researcher-panel failures; the 120,832-step endpoint added three further task-reference failures. Joint-configuration shaping therefore did not measurably resolve the targeted cases under that transferred recipe, although the fixed panels cannot isolate reward shaping from transfer or optimization. The observation representation includes errors to both valid inverse-kinematics branches, while the reward directly shapes Cartesian progress and hold completion. Transfer compatibility is supported by the unchanged robot, action mapping, target geometry, observation semantics and network shape, but fixed 200-episode panels remain development evidence and are not the official 200-episode assessment.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether the residual failures reflect underrepresented target regions, PPO optimization dynamics, or a limitation of the transferred policy. It is also unknown whether a policy that improves those regions preserves broad success and whether any development-panel gain generalizes to the official final assessment.
